title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the sh wrapper keeps empty, '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, so its bare-name tools (git, dirname, uname, serena) and a standalone moe-call.sh can run project copies
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review. It covers residuals 1 and 2 in architect-54e5eb09's comment-1deae51a and the "POSIX pwsh does not prepend the pinned dir" residual from task-64809b19's review.

Evidence at 28df02f7: moe-agent.sh under the marker pins node and python3 (protected_pin_interpreters) and the agent CLI (protected_path_lookup), but it leaves PATH as inherited. Every other bare-name command, such as git, dirname, uname, mktemp and the Serena binary, is still found by PATH lookup, so an empty, '.', relative or in-project entry reaches a project-planted copy. A standalone `scripts/moe-call.sh` under the marker runs `command -v node`, and only the wrapper's use_node prepend makes that safe. The pwsh (POSIX) path of moe-agent.ps1 aliases node but does not prepend its directory.

Fix direction: under the marker, rewrite PATH once, early, to the absolute entries outside the project (the same test protected_path_lookup applies), before any bare-name call. moe-call.sh does the same, or it refuses to run under the marker without a pinned node.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, moe-agent.sh and moe-call.sh drop empty, '.', relative and in-project PATH entries before their first bare-name command; a planted <project>/git (or dirname) on a '.' entry never runs, proved by a bash row like protected-agent-command.test.mjs N5.
The ps1 POSIX (pwsh) path gives child processes the pinned node directory first, or the row documents why it is not needed.
Legacy seats are unchanged; parity-check.sh and the launcher suites exit 0.
reopenReason: Human "move from backlog": CQ-RF07 residual (sh wrapper keeps unsafe PATH entries under the protected marker).

comments.author: worker-c9368191
comments.content:
Planner input from CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), epic-final review, finding 4 (LOW). It belongs with this row's "PATH as inherited" class.

Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-call.sh never remove `NODE_OPTIONS` or `NODE_PATH` (grep finds no hit in any of the three at 28df02f7). The IDEs do remove both before spawning the installed daemon: MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt 576-581, and MoeDaemonClient.ts 537 and 562.

So the pinned node that the wrapper runs (the proxy, moe-call, helper .mjs scripts) still honours an inherited `NODE_OPTIONS=--require ./x.js`. That path is resolved against the seat's cwd, which is the project.

The values come from the user's own environment rather than the repository, which is why this is LOW. Still, for parity, drop both variables in the same early protected block that rewrites PATH, in sh and ps1, and add one row that sets NODE_OPTIONS to a planted require and asserts it never loads.

comments.author: architect-24611a0a
comments.content:
Architect note for this row's planner: it now dependsOn task-2f22237b (WORKING), and here is why.

task-2f22237b adds, right after the marker is read:
- `if [ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" = 1 ]; then export NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1; fi` at moe-agent.sh:51;
- `if ($script:MoeRuntimeProtected) { $env:NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1' }` at moe-agent.ps1:469;
- rows C1 and C2 at the end of scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs, plus run() changes: a `role` option and a widened env filter.

Your early PATH rewrite would sit on the same lines, so rebase conflicts were likely. Plan on top of its landed bytes.

Useful for your RED rows: a worker-role run in that fixture never launches the CLI (MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=claim-failed). Use `run(..., { role: 'governor' })`, which launches it with the inert runtime, and on Windows add git's folder to PATH for the agent Git guard. See Serena mem gotcha-protected-agent-command-reaching-the-cli.
